# The Mosaic SDUI vocabulary

**Version 3.1.0.** This is the whole of what a client must implement and what a
producer may emit. It is generated from `ui.spec.json`, so it cannot disagree
with the bindings, the conformance fixture or the corpus — all four come from
that one file.

Three tiers, and the difference between them is what a change costs:

| Tier | What it is | Cost of adding one |
|---|---|---|
| **Primitives** (25) | Native code every client implements | A client release, on every platform |
| **Components** (44) | Definitions the Platform serves as data | Nothing — a file in `definitions/` |
| **Actions** (12) | Behaviours a client interprets | A client release |

## Type names

A core type is unprefixed. A module's own type is `moduleId:type`, and a core
type never contains `:`. Without the namespace two modules could both
contribute a `StatChip`, and one could contribute a `PosterCard` and take the
core component's place in every client's registry.

## Prop values

A prop is a literal, or a binding: `{"$bind": "path"}`, resolved where the node
renders. A binding names a path and nothing else — no formatting, no default,
no expression. Formatting is server-side, which is why no client needs an
evaluator. An object carrying `$bind` beside any other key is a literal object.

## Primitives

Every one carries the reason a definition cannot express it. That justification
is required, because growing this tier is the only vocabulary change that costs
a release on every platform at once.

### `Box`

Box is the layout container every composition is built from.

*Native because:* The irreducible layout leaf. A definition is a tree of primitives, so the base case cannot itself be a definition. It also resolves style.responsive against the live viewport, and visibleWhen against the live State scope — two render-time branches no static tree can carry.

*Tier:* presentational · *Renders children:* true

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `boxStyle` | Layout and surface style, including the responsive override. |
| `visibleWhen` | `predicate` | Structured predicate over the enclosing State scope's values; absent means always visible. On a field it hides one control, and on a Box it hides a whole branch — which is what makes a multi-step form expressible at all. Without it a wizard is either one long page or a round trip per step, and a round trip per step means every step's answers travel back down in the next tree. |

### `Text`

Text renders a run of text in a token style. Children render after the text, for inline nesting.

*Native because:* The irreducible text leaf.

*Tier:* presentational · *Renders children:* true

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `string` | The string to render. |
| `style` | `textStyle` | Variant, weight and colour token. |

### `Image`

Image renders a remote or proxied image with a placeholder fallback.

*Native because:* Loading a resource, handling decode failure and falling back to a placeholder are client behaviours. It also feeds the art-light sampler, which reads decoded pixels.

*Tier:* presentational · *Renders children:* false

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `src` | `string` | Image URL. Platform-emitted URLs are artwork-proxy signed. |
| `alt` | `string` | Alternative text. |
| `fit` | `enum:cover|contain` | How the image fills its box. |
| `placeholder` | `string` | Text shown while loading or when the source fails. |
| `placeholderMode` | `enum:label|initials` | Whether the placeholder renders as a label or as initials. |
| `artLight` | `enum:ambient|focus` | Publish this image's palette to the acrylic surfaces. |
| `motion` | `enum:drift` | Slowly scale and pan the image behind its frame, so a still backdrop reads as a live surface rather than a photograph. A client that honours prefers-reduced-motion holds it still. |
| `style` | `boxStyle` | Box style applied to the image frame. |

### `Icon`

Icon renders one glyph from the client's bundled icon set.

*Native because:* Resolves a name to a vector the client ships. The glyph set is a client asset, not data.

*Tier:* presentational · *Renders children:* false

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `iconName` | Icon name from the shared set. |
| `size` | `string|number` | Rendered size; defaults to 1.2em. |
| `color` | `colorToken` | Colour token override. |

### `Pressable`

Pressable makes its subtree activate an Action.

*Native because:* Turning a pointer, key or remote-control event into an Action dispatch is client behaviour.

*Tier:* interactive · *Renders children:* true

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `boxStyle` | Layout and surface style, including the responsive override. |
| `action` | `action` | Action emitted on activation. |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | Refuse activation and render the disabled state. |
| `lift` | `boolean` | Apply the hover-lift affordance. |
| `label` | `string` | Accessible label when the subtree carries no text. |

### `Spacer`

Spacer occupies empty space in a stack, fixed or growing.

*Native because:* An irreducible layout leaf.

*Tier:* presentational · *Renders children:* false

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `size` | `spaceToken` | Fixed size from the space scale. |
| `grow` | `boolean` | Absorb the remaining free space instead. |

### `Fragment`

Fragment renders its children with no wrapper of its own.

*Native because:* A transparent grouping node the expander needs in order to return several nodes where one is expected.

*Tier:* presentational · *Renders children:* true

### `Outlet`

Outlet marks the point in a definition's template where the caller's slot content is substituted.

*Native because:* It is the definition expander's own mechanism. A definition defined in terms of Outlet cannot itself be expanded without it, so it must be native.

*Tier:* presentational · *Renders children:* true

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | Slot name filled from the caller's slots map. |

### `NavItem`

NavItem is one entry in the app frame's navigation.

*Native because:* Owns active-route state: it compares the current screen against its own target, which only the client knows.

*Tier:* interactive · *Renders children:* false

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `label` | `string` | Visible label. |
| `icon` | `iconName` | Leading icon. |
| `screen` | `string` | Screen this item marks as active. |
| `action` | `action` | Action emitted on activation. |

### `NavBar`

NavBar groups NavItems into the frame's responsive navigation.

*Native because:* Presents as an inline bar or a bottom tab strip depending on the viewport — a render-time branch, not data.

*Tier:* interactive · *Renders children:* true

### `Tabs`

Tabs shows one panel at a time behind a tab strip. Each tab's content goes in the named slot matching its id, not in the ordered child list — an ordered child is dropped.

*Native because:* Owns the active tab index.

*Tier:* interactive · *Renders children:* false

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `tabs` | `array:tab` | Tab descriptors, each an id and a label. |

### `Rotator`

Rotator cross-fades through its children on a timer.

*Native because:* Owns a timer and derives the active index from it, and republishes the active slide's palette to the acrylic surfaces.

*Tier:* interactive · *Renders children:* true

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `interval` | `number` | Dwell time per slide in milliseconds. |

### `State`

State declares named variables and scopes them to its subtree. Children bind to them by name, and a setValue action writes them.

*Native because:* It holds values across renders. A tree is a description of one moment; something has to remember what was typed between two of them, and no arrangement of static nodes can. It is also the scope boundary itself — which of two enclosing States a name resolves to is a question only the renderer, walking its own tree, can answer.

*Tier:* interactive · *Renders children:* true

| Prop | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `vars` | `array:stateVar` | The variables this scope declares: each a name, a type (string, number or boolean) and an initial value. Declared rather than inferred so a client knows a name exists before anything writes to it, and knows what to coerce a written value to. |

## Components

Served as data (`definitions/*.json`). A client implements none of them; it
expands whatever it is sent.

- **`Screen`** — Screen is the root of a server-defined page.
- **`Section`** — Section is a titled band.
- **`Carousel`** — Carousel is a horizontal snap-scrolling rail.
- **`Grid`** — Grid is a responsive auto-fill grid.
- **`Stack`** — Stack arranges children; direction is "horizontal" or "vertical".
- **`HeroBanner`** — Hero is a featured banner. Fill its call-to-action row with Actions.
- **`PosterCard`** — PosterCard renders a work/item card.
- **`Button`** — Button carries an action; variant is primary/secondary/ghost/danger.
- **`Badge`** — Badge is a small pill; tone is one of the Tone values.
- **`Banner`** — Banner is an inline message; tone is one of the Tone values.
- **`DetailHeader`** — DetailHeader renders a node's metadata (title, meta, genres).
- **`EpisodeRow`** — EpisodeRow renders one episode under a season.
- **`PersonChip`** — PersonChip is a cast/crew chip.
- **`GenreTag`** — GenreTag is a genre chip.
- **`FilterChip`** — FilterChip is one selectable narrowing on a browse surface: a pressable pill that draws its own selected state, with an optional count of what it would leave.
- **`EmptyState`** — EmptyState is a titled empty placeholder, with an optional explanation beneath it and a call to action.
- **`AppShell`** — AppShell is the application frame (ADR 0031): the brand bar, the nav and the region the current screen renders into.
- **`DetailHero`** — DetailHero is a title's cinematic header — backdrop, logo and the actions docked over it.
- **`Divider`** — Divider is a rule, optionally labelled.
- **`ErrorState`** — ErrorState renders a Platform error category as something a person can act on.
- **`ExtensionCard`** — ExtensionCard is one extension module — what it is, what it can do, and where its bytes come from (ADR 0081).
- **`IconButton`** — IconButton is a Button reduced to its icon; the label stays for assistive tech.
- **`InfoPanel`** — InfoPanel is a docked facts panel — a rating and a run of label/value rows. The mockups draw a control under it ("Change device"); it is not here because Mosaic has no device registry to change between, and a panel is the wrong place to learn that.
- **`FactCard`** — FactCard is one labelled card in a row of technical facts — what a release is, how it will be delivered, where its metadata came from. Distinct from InfoPanel because the shape is different and so is the job: a panel answers about the title in label/value pairs, a card states three short facts about one aspect of it and sits in a grid of siblings.
- **`MediaTile`** — MediaTile is a landscape card for episodes and continue-watching.
- **`Pagination`** — Pagination is a prev/next pair. The server supplies both targets; the client does no arithmetic.
- **`PlaybackBar`** — PlaybackBar is the resume strip for something already started.
- **`RelatedRail`** — RelatedRail is a titled rail that says so when it is empty.
- **`Select`** — Select is a labelled dropdown over server-supplied options.
- **`SettingsFrame`** — SettingsFrame is the Platform-owned settings chrome (ADR 0038): a nav beside the panel the open section fills.
- **`SpanRow`** — SpanRow is one span of a waterfall: its name, indented by depth, a bar showing its share of the whole, and its duration. The share is the point — a waterfall exists to answer which part of this was the time, and a duration alone does not.
- **`DetailPanel`** — DetailPanel is a titled working surface: a header carrying a name, an identifier and a summary, over a body. Flat rather than acrylic — it is the administrative side of the app, where there is no artwork behind the surface for the material to bend.
- **`StatCard`** — StatCard is one figure with a name over it — a percentile, an error rate, a throughput. Distinct from FactCard, which states three short sentences about an aspect of something; this states one number and exists to be scanned in a row of its siblings.
- **`LogTable`** — LogTable is a run of structured records as a table — time, level, service, message and the trace that produced it, in fixed columns. A table rather than a stack of cards because the columns are how you read a log: the eye runs down one of them looking for the line that is different.
- **`LatencyHistogram`** — LatencyHistogram is a distribution as bars — where the time actually went, which a set of percentiles summarises and cannot show. Bars carry their own count and label; the server sizes them, because only it knows what the tallest bucket is.
- **`TraceRow`** — TraceRow is one trace in a list: what ran, its id, how long it took, and a status dot when something inside it failed.
- **`SettingsRow`** — SettingsRow is one line of a settings panel — a label, an optional explanation of what it does, and a control or a value on the right. It is the workhorse of every panel in the design, which is why it is a component rather than a Stack assembled per screen: a panel that builds its own rows is a panel that drifts from the others.
- **`SettingsNavGroup`** — SettingsNavGroup is one labelled run of settings nav rows.
- **`SettingsNavItem`** — SettingsNavItem is one settings nav row. The server marks the active one — it is the side that knows the params (ADR 0039).
- **`SourcePicker`** — SourcePicker lists the resolved sources for a Part.
- **`StatusIndicator`** — StatusIndicator is a coloured dot with a label.
- **`TextField`** — TextField is a labelled text input with optional help.
- **`Toggle`** — Toggle is a switch with a label. It carries the value it moves TO — the client reports the flip, the server decides what it means.
- **`Form`** — Form is a State scope with a submit control: it declares the fields' variables, hosts them, and emits its submit action with their values merged in. Composed rather than native — it is a State, an Outlet and a button, and nothing about it needs client code.

## Actions

| Kind | What it does |
|---|---|
| `navigate` | Navigate pushes a screen, optionally with params. |
| `invoke` | Invoke runs a server mutation, optionally with input. |
| `playPart` | Play starts playback of a part. |
| `openUrl` | OpenURL opens an external URL (the client validates the scheme). |
| `back` | Back returns to the previous screen. |
| `query` | Query re-reads a screen's data without changing the route. |
| `openOverlay` | OpenOverlay presents a node as a modal, sheet or drawer. |
| `closeOverlay` | CloseOverlay dismisses the topmost overlay. |
| `toast` | Toast shows a transient message. |
| `sequence` | Sequence runs several actions in order, stopping at the first failure. |
| `setValue` | SetValue writes a value into a named field in the enclosing form scope. |
| `submit` | Submit runs an action with the enclosing State scope's values merged into its input. `field` names where they merge — a path into the input, or empty for its top level. |

## Closed sets

Each of these is closed, and closed in the same direction: the server may name
only what every client can interpret. An open set lets the server state
something a client silently ignores, which fails open.

**Validators** — a rule the server states and the client enforces. The server
enforces everything again; the client's copy is what saves the round trip.

| Validator | Argument | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `required` | `boolean` | The field must be non-empty. |
| `minLength` | `number` | Minimum length in characters. |
| `maxLength` | `number` | Maximum length in characters. |
| `pattern` | `string` | RE2 regular expression the value must match. RE2 rather than PCRE so every client can compile it and none can be made to backtrack. |
| `matches` | `string` | Another field's name whose value this must equal — the confirm-password case. |
| `oneOf` | `array:string` | The value must be one of these. |

**Predicates** — conditions over scope values, as `visibleWhen` uses. An
unreadable predicate is **false**: a control shown because its rule could not
be read is the failure that reveals things.

| Predicate | Shape |
|---|---|
| `equals` | {field, equals} — the named field's value equals this. |
| `notEmpty` | {field, notEmpty: true} — the named field has a value. |
| `oneOf` | {field, oneOf: [...]} — the named field is one of these. |
| `not` | {not: <predicate>} — negation. |
| `all` | {all: [<predicate>...]} — conjunction. |
| `any` | {any: [<predicate>...]} — disjunction. |

**Roles** — mapped, not passed through: ARIA on the web, a semantics property
in Compose, a trait in SwiftUI. A role a client maps to nothing is a control
invisible to a screen reader and correct-looking to everyone else.

`alert` · `button` · `dialog` · `group` · `heading` · `img` · `link` · `list` · `listitem` · `main` · `navigation` · `none` · `progressbar` · `region` · `search` · `status` · `tab` · `tablist` · `tabpanel`

**Focus directions** — what a `nextFocus` override may name. No diagonals: no
remote has them.

`up` · `down` · `left` · `right`

**Tones**

`neutral` · `accent` · `success` · `warning` · `danger` · `info`

**Overlay surfaces**

`modal` · `sheet` · `drawer`

## Proving a client implements this

`conformance/vocabulary.json` is this document as data — the sets a client
declares itself against. `conformance/cases/*.json` is the corpus: golden
inputs and outputs for validators, predicates, binding resolution and
definition expansion. A client that passes the corpus behaves like the ones
that exist; a client that does not knows exactly where it differs.
